subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when a request comes from a configured trusted proxy but the configured identity header is absent?
rationale: The requested behavior changes who OpenClaw authenticates as when the upstream proxy provides no per-user identity, affecting Gateway authorization, Control UI access, session scoping, and operator trust boundaries.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed
options.body: Continue rejecting missing identity headers and document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that forwards identity.

options.title: Accept Narrow Fallback
options.body: Add an explicit fallback identity only with strict config, proxy-owned required headers or signed assertions, allowUsers validation, loopback/origin rules, audit warnings, and regression tests.

options.title: Defer To Auth Redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open as input for a broader identity-bearing proxy policy instead of adding a one-off fallback key now.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Continue rejecting missing identity headers and document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that forwards identity.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have the clearest recent routing and implementation history for this trusted-proxy auth cluster.
